updates.before:
- Run a final privacy/secret scan across all candidate bodies before writing back verdicts.
- Clean up temporary verification scripts after completion so only cache intermediates remain.
- When the OpenViking writeback apply runs slowly in the background, do not guess or stitch a job id; use job_list to obtain the real id and poll until completion before reporting.
- When a writeback apply takes a long time, do not diagnose a hang prematurely: check the script logic first (each item needs several ov CLI reads/writes, about 135 calls and roughly 12 seconds per item for 45 items); when the process is not visible but the job is still running, do not judge progress from aggregate audit_status counts (mostly historical rounds), instead read the last_checked timestamps of the first and last URI in the current round to confirm persistence and spot-check middle items to estimate remaining time.
- Use a script to read uri/sha from select.json and merge verdicts into result.json, avoiding manual transcription of all entries.
- When the script indexes verdict notes by 1-based position, do not insert missing keys in the middle of the dictionary (it misaligns all later keys); instead adjust the read index (for example base[i+1]) and undo the insertion.
- Confirm the apply script path before writeback: the script is in the project scripts/ directory and the working directory is D:/repository/skills, to avoid path errors.
- result.json is an array; each verdict record contains uri, verdict, note, and body_sha256_16 fields; apply maps and writes back each item by these fields.

- Run a final privacy/secret scan across all candidate bodies before writing back verdicts.
- Clean up temporary verification scripts after completion so only cache intermediates remain.
- When the OpenViking writeback apply runs slowly in the background, do not guess or stitch a job id; use job_list to obtain the real id and poll until completion before reporting.
- When a writeback apply takes a long time, do not diagnose a hang prematurely: check the script logic first (each item needs several ov CLI reads/writes, about 135 calls and roughly 12 seconds per item for 45 items); when the process is not visible but the job is still running, do not judge progress from aggregate audit_status counts (mostly historical rounds), instead read the last_checked timestamps of the first and last URI in the current round to confirm persistence and spot-check middle items to estimate remaining time.
- Use a script to read uri/sha from select.json and merge verdicts into result.json, avoiding manual transcription of all entries.
- When the script indexes verdict notes by 1-based position, do not insert missing keys in the middle of the dictionary (it misaligns all later keys); instead adjust the read index (for example base[i+1]) and undo the insertion.
- Confirm the apply script path before writeback: the script is in the project scripts/ directory and the working directory is D:/repository/skills, to avoid path errors.
- result.json is an array; each verdict record contains uri, verdict, note, and body_sha256_16 fields; apply maps and writes back each item by these fields.
- When a candidate URI contains spaces, OpenViking writeback normalizes them to underscores and writes to a new URI, so readback verification fails and the item is skipped with its original frontmatter unchanged; this also creates duplicate files and increases the total memory count by the number of skipped items.

updates.before:
- Present the audit report as a table: include total memory count, eligible pool size, sampled/picked count and cooldown window, applied/skipped/verify-ok writeback counts, VALID/INVALID distribution, code-evidence rationale for each entry, list every invalid memory filename separately, remaining unaudited count calculated from the eligible pool minus applied writebacks, cumulative audited count, and coverage percentage.
- When one item is skipped, report both the writeback-based verdict distribution and the full `result.json` verdict distribution; explicitly note that the skipped item remains in the candidate pool.
- Report `post_persist_embedding_err` entries as embedding rebuild errors after writeback; if frontmatter readback passes, state that they do not change the audit verdict.
- For invalid entries, explicitly state whether the target file exists but decisive symbols have zero real-code hits or were found only in memory mirrors.
- When total memory count changes after reindexing on writeback, report both the select-time count and post-writeback count with the reason for the difference.
- State the audit scope explicitly: memory body semantics were not changed, no memories were deleted, no git commit was made, and intermediate files are cache artifacts under `~/.dsh/cache/memory-audit/`.
